rubriker.title: Carlsen Calls Sindarov Significant Favorite Against Gukesh Rules Out Comeback
Samarkand R1 (women): Nine teams from the top ten score 4-0 victories
rubriker._rss_content: India began their women's Chess Olympiad title defence in Samarkand as the top seeds, ahead of Georgia, Kazakhstan, China and the United States. The leading teams made a comfortable start, with nine of the top ten seeds winning 4–0 and no major upsets on individual boards. England's 11-year-old top board Bodhana Sivanandan also opened with a win, defeating Hanna Wilson of Barbados. | Photo: Michal Walusza / FIDE

rubriker.title: Samarkand R1 (open): Favourites win comfortably, Thailand's Laohawirapap upsets Erigaisi
rubriker._rss_content: The 46th Chess Olympiad began in Samarkand with 206 teams in the open section, where the United States, India, Uzbekistan and China are the leading seeds. The top 30 teams all won their opening matches, though a few strong grandmasters dropped points. Botswana produced the only team upset by holding Brazil to a draw, while Arjun Erigaisi suffered the biggest individual upset of the day, losing to Thailand's IM Prin Laohawirapap (pictured). | Photo: Rafal Oleksiewicz / FIDE

rubriker.title: That time Uzbekistan surprisingly won silver at the 1992 Chess Olympiad
rubriker._rss_content: The 1992 Chess Olympiad in Manila was the first held after the dissolution of the Soviet Union. Suddenly, instead of one dominant USSR team, there were several very strong teams representing former Soviet republics. Russia continued the Soviet Union's run of success. The surprise team from Uzbekistan, with just one grandmaster, took silver ahead of Armenia. In the women's event, Georgia won the gold medal. | Photo: Gerhard Hund

rubriker.title: Pakistan Forfeits Round One Match Against Israel at the Olympiad
rubriker._rss_content: Pakistan did not show up for its scheduled Round 1 match against Israel at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, leaving all four boards unplayed and handing Israel a 4-0 walkover.

rubriker.title: FIDE Recaps Day 1 of the Olympiad
rubriker._rss_content: The 46th Chess Olympiad opened in Samarkand with 207 teams in the Open section and 191 in the Women's, and while most of the day went exactly the way the ratings predicted, round one still found room for a genuine shock at the very top of the field.

rubriker.title: FIDE Responds to Visa Issues, but Questions Grow Over Its Handling of the 2026 Olympiad
rubriker._rss_content: FIDE’s response to the Samarkand visa controversy has done little to silence questions over whether the federation was adequately prepared to manage the logistical demands of its own flagship event.

rubriker.title: Rosenstein Raises Alarm Over Last-Minute FIDE Election Changes while FIDE Blames Local Organizers for Disorganization
rubriker._rss_content: FIDE presidential candidate Wadim Rosenstein has stated that FIDE is considering last-minute changes to the upcoming election while shifting responsibility for organizational problems in Samarkand onto local organizers.

rubriker.title: The Drama Continues: Team Montenegro Denied Rooms
rubriker._rss_content: India's hotel troubles in Samarkand weren't an isolated incident. A leaked email and a pointed public post from a longtime chess administrator suggest the Olympiad's accommodation problems reached considerably further than one delegation, and raise real questions about who was actually responsible for fixing it.

rubriker.title: PISA 2025 y la emergencia cognitiva
rubriker._rss_content: Los resultados del informe PISA 2025 vuelven a poner el foco en dos competencias esenciales: la lectura y las matemáticas, que registran niveles históricamente bajos en numerosos sistemas educativos. El texto analiza este deterioro, sus vínculos con la distracción digital, las desigualdades y la formación docente, y plantea al ajedrez como una herramienta afín al razonamiento matemático, la comprensión, la atención sostenida y la resolución de problemas. | Imagen (IA): Uvencio Blanco
